doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Two-week modules and progressive keys
summary: The syllabus runs in two-week modules by key, starting with C and G, building discipline and evenness of tone.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: So I developed this — eventually I developed this syllabus. And the syllabus was to put everybody in the same course so that they had the same materials that they had to know as a graduating trumpet player or band director, and/or band director. You see what I mean? So that this way — now that said, the materials that you had to be tested on, and it’s in two-week modules — so the first week they come in and I say, “Well how did you do on the materials this week?” Because that’s the first week. See? Like so in other words you had two-week modules, the same material. That’s the only time you get to do that material. Then you get tested on it the second week. But if they’re a student, okay, that is fairly advanced. If they took private lessons they’re going to sail through the first stuff, except for maybe the things that they don’t do so well like, “You know your articulation is really not that good. You can play faster than lightening but you know but it’s not really clear what you’re doing.” So you can use them — especially if you use material that is familiar, very familiar to the teacher. You uncover those problems much easier, see? And then you can get right to the root of the problem on the same material. Now the next person I might say, “Well gee your lip slurs on that piece are, you know you really don’t have the right air, so let’s work on that to make sure that you have a tone line, that it doesn’t sound like” [scats]. I said, “Do you talk like that? Let’s go eat.” “Okay.” I said, “You don’t talk like that, do you?” I said, “I’m not making fun of you but” I said, “that’s what music is, people hear you and they have to understand what you’re saying. And the way they do that is through the evenness of your voice.” So we have to create that and so all these materials, and then at the same time those materials in the first two weeks are only in C and G. It was — because they were familiar with those keys. I want to put them at ease. I don’t want them to feel like you’re going to do C and C sharp today. These first two weeks. And they play C and they feel good and then they play C sharp and they can’t even play the scale. See? So I wanted to make sure it was progressive. You know it progressed to — they were learning discipline training, because they only had two weeks to learn the materials. Then they went away and they had the next two weeks, F and D. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

See what I mean? So you’re adding accidentals and you’re adding the appropriate etudes that are in those keys. So they’re playing like in that key for two weeks. They don’t have other keys. And then they have to learn it. So the reason, once again, is to put everybody on an even keel. When you go to English class and you’re the worst reader in the class it takes you longer to read the books. It takes you longer to understand reading faster what’s going on. It takes you longer to understand the plot or whatever, whatever your weakness is. But hopefully the materials, if they’re chosen right by the teacher, will allow you to start figuring out what needs the most work. Of course you go to lessons and that’s really what we talk about.
